title: Integrity
content:
Goal:

Implement policies and procedures to protect electronic protected health information from improper alteration or destruction.

Implementation specification:  Mechanism to authenticate electronic protected health information (Addressable). Implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that electronic protected health information has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized  manner.

Policy Statement

HUBzero must include considerations in its Software Management Plan, Incident Response Plan, filesystem Security Model, and Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan that support integrity by preventing, detecting and remediating the alteration or destruction of data.

HUBzero should, wherever practical, use good practices that maintain the integrity of data, such as database foreign key constraints.  In addition, where such implementation will not duplicate already existing controls provided by a computing environment (e.g., SDSC Sherlock or AWS), HUBzero must implement the minimum requirements of the NIST control family "SI System and Information Integrity", in controls SI-1, SI-2, SI-3, SI-4, SI-5 and SI-12.

Implementation

Fail2ban will be employed to monitor ssh logs, apache logs, and the mail system, which are all login mechanisms. The integrity of system packages will be verified at least quarterly by using utilities provided by the operating system. In addition, in the HUBzero "publications" functionality, publications will be stored with a hash for integrity verification purposes.

HUBzero will attempt to detect system-level attacks as described in the other technical safeguard sections (164.312). HUBzero’s response to successful unauthorized modification or destruction of EPHI is to restore data from the last backup, as described in the Incident Response Plan, and if applicable, the Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan.

Custom applications developed for a particular hub must implement their own protection scheme (e.g., database foreign key constraints, hashes, etc...) to protect EPHI information, as appropriate for the application.  Developers of applications hosted on HUBzero infrastructure should develop procedures for detecting attempts to modify or destroy EPHI by attacking the application.

 

For historical purposes, an old version of this policy is stored in the old wiki.

title: Workforce Security
content:
Goal:

Implement policies and procedures to ensure that all members of its workforce have appropriate access to electronic protected health information, as provided under paragraph (a)(4) of this section, and to prevent those workforce members who do not have access under paragraph (a)(4) of this section from obtaining access to electronic protected health information.

Background

HUBzero staff that have administrative rights (“privileged access”) to the systems containing EPHI are covered by the following policies. That is because they could modify the system or application code that is used to store, process, transform, and/or modify EPHI and through that action expose the EPHI to unauthorized individuals. The exposure could be accidental (through a configuration change) or intentional (through modification of source code).
For example, being root or a member of www-data means that they can potentially capture the unencrypted EPHI as the forms are being submitted. Even after EPHI has been encrypted, the encryption key is available to people with this type of privileged access, so in effect they have full access. Superusers in the web interface at "/administrator". Paragraph (a) (4) Information Access Management policies and procedures define privileged access. “Workforce member” below refers to HUBzero staff only.


Authorization And/Or Supervision

1. HUBzero shall ensure that HUBzero workforce members who have the ability to access EPHI or work in areas where EPHI might be accessed, shall be properly authorized and/or supervised.


2. HUBzero will define and maintain processes for granting authorization and access to EPHI, including:

a. Procedure for permitting access to EPHI
b. Procedure for logging and tracking authorization of access to EPHI.
c. Procedure for reviewing and revising, on a periodic basis, authorization of access to EPHI (the periodic basis is to be defined in the documentation of that process).
The above are documented at 164.308 a 4 Information Access Management, Access Authorization.

3. Workforce members shall not be allowed access to EPHI or to areas where EPHI might be accessed until proper authorization is granted.

4. Only authorized workforce members who have need for privileged access in order to fulfill their respective job responsibilities shall be authorized to access EPHI or areas where EPHI might be accessed. HUBzero shall review access levels on a periodic basis and make revisions as necessary. HUBzero shall establish a procedure for reviewing and revising, on a periodic basis, authorization of access to EPHI or to areas where EPHI might be accessed.

The above-mentioned procedure is documented at 164.308 a 4 Information Access Management, Access Establishment and Modification.


Workforce Clearance Procedure


1. HUBzero shall take reasonable and appropriate steps to ensure that workforce members have the appropriate authorization to access EPHI.

See 164.308 a 4 Information Access Management, Access Authorization.

2. HUBzero managers, system administrators and the HIPAA liaison will work together to identify which HUBzero employees are allowed to grant privileged access to other workforce members or supervise them.


3. HUBzero will rely on SDSC Human Resources to review prospective workforce members’ backgrounds during the hiring process.


Policy for Termination Procedures

Detailed termination procedures are maintained at https://hubzero.org/groups/production/wiki/TerminationProcs

For the purposes of termination procedures, hubs have at least 2 kinds of users: SDSC employees and others.

San Diego Supercomputing Center (SDSC) Employees

Access privileges will be removed or disabled as soon as possible upon notification from an employee’s supervisor that the access is no longer needed. If the employee has ceased work and a public notice of termination is published before an employee’s supervisor or a hub owner specifies which access should be preserved, it must be assumed that no access is needed anymore.


Other employees

Access credentials of hub users that aren’t Purdue employees will be removed or disabled as soon as possible upon notification from a credible and authoritative source (e.g., the owner of a hub) that the access is no longer needed or that it should be withdrawn.

It should be noted that the objective of these termination procedures is not to remove all access, but to *reduce* access privileges to those enjoyed by regular hub users, unless complete removal is desired for disciplinary reasons (e.g., as a consequence of policy violations). Thus, accounts themselves should normally not be disabled or closed, although closing accounts used solely in the course of employment (e.g., test accounts) is appropriate. It is problematic to determine exactly which access a terminated employee should have as a regular hub user; when in doubt, group memberships and other privileges must be removed. Hub owners or group managers can later grant access back. The act of removing and granting access later based on the new, regular hub user status shows that due diligence was done and provides assurance that the access privileges are correct.

Responsibility for Applying the Termination Procedures

Hubzero staff are responsible for applying the policy for prior employees. Otherwise, hub owners and their staff are responsible for applying the policy for their own staff, students and anyone to whom they have granted privileges.

title: Web Application Vulnerability Scanning
content:
HUBzero uses the service "Detectify" provided at "detectify.com" to perform vulnerability scanning.  Each HIPAA-covered hub should have a dedicated "scan profile" on the service, and each scan will be recorded separately.  The following procedure is for production servers;  vulnerabilities found on non-production servers that have restricted access, and that do not exist on a production server, should be given less priority, depending on circumstances.

  • Go to the dashboard, https://detectify.com/dashboard and login if needed
  • Go to "Assets" and click "Add asset".  Select the manual method and enter the domain name of the hub.
  • To create a scan profile, select an asset, and the "Scan profiles" tab.  Click on "Create Scan profiles"
  • Configure profiles by clicking on "
    • Scan profile settings (tab)
      • How often do you want to run a scan?  Should be set to "Recurring scans:  every month"
      • Should we automatically start a scan when new security tests are added?    Yes
      • How long should we keep the reports before deleting? 90 days
      • Opt-in for the following beta features
        • Missing security header
        • Run missing security header tests against all paths
    • Deep Scan Settings (tab)
      • Should we crawl subdomains?  YEs
      • Which subdomains must we avoid? None
      • Which paths/URLs must we include?
        • /administrator
        • /api
        • /app/site
        • /app/templates
        • /infrastructure
        • /tools
        • /webdav
      • Should we scan common ports?  Yes
      • Which ports must we avoid? None
      • Which predefined analytics services should we avoid? (Only avoid Google and Twitter)
      • How should the scanners be recognizable?  Use the Detectify user agent.  Do not attempt to define and MSIE user agent to avoid the false positives for IE-only XSS, because then the scanner will be completely banned from the site!
      • How fast can we go? 100 requests/second
         
  • When notified that a scan has ended, check scan results from the dashboard, by clicking on the links "Finished..."
    • Analyze the findings by severity
      • Try to reproduce the finding from the URL and any submitted POST data, to remove false positives
      • Determine if this affects only the hub where it was reported, or if it's something that affects all hubs
      • Determine if this is something that could be fixed by changing the configuration of services like Apache, the configuration of the HUBzero CMS, or if it is a code issue
    • Create Trello cards:
      • in the "Sprint" board for findings with CVSS >9 scores and label them as an "incursion"
        • Request from a manager that the card be assigned ASAP to someone available with appropriate skills
        • If a code update is not scheduled within a week and this is a code issue, ask a Communications Manager to contact the affected hubs about the issue, with the goal of determining if patching needs to be scheduled
        • If this is a configuration issue, a system administrator will implement the change through Ansible
          • If it can be fixed simply by restarting a service like Apache, determine an appropriate time and do it after notifying other system administrators and the Slack "trouble" channel
          • If more involved tasks are involved, a special time may need to be scheduled.  Ask a Communications Manager to help
      • in the "Backlog" board for other vulnerabilities
        • label "High" impact vulnerabilities with CVSS scores <=9 as "Next Sprint"
        • label all vulnerabilities as "security"
    • For FISMA-Low certified hubs, additionally the actions and timelines described in control (CA-5) "Plan of Action and Milestones" must be followed.
    • Control SI-2 "Flaw Remediation" also requires the following timelines for resolution:
      • "The following remediation timelines must be met, or the affected device may be removed from the network:"
        • Critical within 30 days;
        • High within 60 days;
        • Medium within 1 year; and
        • Low within 1 year.
    • If a hub has a FISMA certification other than plain baseline Low, refer to its SSP (System Security Plan) for the appropriate timelines.

title: a 1 ii (B) Risk Management
content:
1. Goal

HUBzero will implement security measures designed to reduce the risks to EPHI to a reasonable level, provided that applications making use of EPHI restrict themselves to an appropriately limited set of HUB features and infrastructure hosts, and communicate this set to HUBzero. Not all HUB functionality and all HUB hosts can be secured to a level appropriate for handling EPHI information. HUBzero cannot alone provide a reasonable risk level for EPHI information without strong cooperation from HUB stakeholders and their considerable involvement in the risk management process.

2. Periodic Risk Management Process Requirements

a. Assessment and prioritization, on the basis of risks, of EPHI Systems.

b. Selection and implementation of reasonable, appropriate, and cost-effective security measures to manage, mitigate, or accept identified risks.

c. Security training and awareness on implemented security measures to relevant workforce members.

d. Periodic evaluation and revision, as necessary, of the security measures.

3. Risk management process

The risk management process for HUBzero systems, excluding the EPHI-handling applications, shall be conducted by HUBzero system administrators in consultation with the staff member most qualified with regards to security concerns, or by that staff member. The developers of applications handling EPHI information need to perform their own risk management, and be aware of the risks involved in their decision to enable and utilize available HUB functionality.

a. Risk analysis ­

The risk analysis required by HIPAA (see 164.308 a 1 ii (A)) is a sound basis for risk management activities. Ticket handling is also a good opportunity to discover risks. Non-trivial issues can be discussed on the “ncn-maint” mailing list if it might help resolve the following steps. HUBzero staff will be available for consultation by developers of applications handling EPHI information.

b. Risk prioritization ­

Risks identified in the risk analysis or otherwise shall be prioritized based on the overall calculated risk level. Amongst issues of equal level, potential impact to HUBzero systems where the existing controls are the weakest and the expected cost of remediation is the lowest shall be used for prioritization. Risks at the highest level should be handled as soon as possible. Responsibility for responding to discovered risks should be passed to an appropriate staff member, e.g., by filing a ticket. Non-confidential, non-urgent risks and their solution can be discussed using the HUBzero Wish system.

c. Method identification ­

The appropriate security methods to minimize or eliminate identified risks shall be identified. Security methods shall be identified based on the nature, feasibility, and effectiveness of the specific security method.

d. Cost-benefit analysis ­

HUBzero shall identify and define the costs and benefits of implementing or not implementing the identified security methods.

e. Security method selection ­

Based on the cost-benefit analysis, HUBzero shall select the most appropriate, reasonable, and cost-effective security methods for reducing the identified risks.

f. Assignment of responsibility ­

HUBzero staff with the appropriate expertise shall implement the selected security methods.

g. Security method implementation ­

The selected security methods shall be properly implemented by the responsible workforce members.

h. Security method evaluation ­

The selected and implemented security methods shall be evaluated and revised, as necessary, by the HUBzero staff member most qualified with regards to security concerns.

4. Strategies for Managing Risk

The strategies for managing risk shall be proportionate with the risks to and sensitivity of EPHI. The security measures shall reasonably protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of EPHI. The following methods are used to manage risk:

a. Situational Awareness

b. Risk acceptance­

c. Risk avoidance­

d. Risk limitation­

e. Risk transference­

4.1 Vulnerability Scanning

Vulnerability scanning is a strategy for situational awareness, and defined as control RA-5 in NIST SP 800-53. There are several types of vulnerability scans.  In the Sherlock environment, network vulnerability scanning, and scanning of the infrastructure, are handled by the Sherlock team.  HUBzero is responsible for "web application scanning" to detect vulnerabilities in the HUBzero software, and will do as follows:

a. Web application scans will be conducted monthly and when new vulnerabilities potentially affecting the system/applications are identified and reported;
b. The scans will identify findings by using the Common Vulnerability and Exposures (CVE) and the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS)
c. Vulnerability scan reports and results from security control assessments will be analyzed;
d. Legitimate vulnerabilities will be remediated in accordance with an NIH or IC risk assessment and per HHS and/or NIH policies
e. The information obtained from the vulnerability scanning process and security control assessments will be shared with the NIH CISO, NIH ISAO, NIH OSOP, and System Owner and IC CIO, ISSO, Privacy Coordinator, and System Owner

HUBzero will document the web application scanning process, with identified roles and responsibilities, incorporating appropriate federal oversight and separation of duties, in the "Procedures" section of the HUBzero documentation.

5. Results

The results of the risk management process shall be documented either in tickets, in the HUBzero wiki for the “production” group or in the software configuration management system’s (currently “Ansible”) comments and settings.

Historical: the risk management policy was documented in the old wiki.

title: a 1 ii A Risk Analysis
content:
HUBzero will take reasonable steps to identify and prioritize the risks to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of EPHI due to HUBzero software and its configuration.  However, the infrastructure provided by the Sherlock environment shall have its own separate risk analysis,  documented separately in the "SDSC Sherlock Risk Assessment Plan", not covered here.  For this purpose, the risk analysis will comprise:

-An inventory of which VMs are covered under HIPAA rules.

-An identification of potential threats to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of EPHI.

-An identification of weaknesses that may facilitate the realization of threats.

-An assessment of existing controls that mitigate the weaknesses.

-An assessment of the likelihood, impact, and overall risk posed by the weaknesses.

-Recommendations.


This analysis shall be updated every year. The results of the risk analysis shall be considered confidential. This means that it will only be shared with non-HUBzero staff on a need-to-know basis. Hard copies shall be kept in reasonably secure locations, and electronic copies shall not be available for public access.

Historical:  the risk analysis policy used at Purdue is in the old wiki.

title: Security Awareness and Training
content:
1. Security Reminders

HUBzero will post security reminders in its Slack workspace, in the "general" channel, reminding the workforce on the importance of protecting PHI.  The HUBzero ISO will select security reminders from blog posts relevant to current activity at HUBzero, from hipaasecuritysuite.com (see https://hipaasecuritysuite.com/hipaa-compliant-security-reminders), or from other appropriate souces.

System administrators will subscribe to at least one security mailing list relevant to the operating systems and software in use.

2. Protection From Malicious Software

2.1 Practices and procedures for malware prevention and detection

The following practices and procedures are to be taught to system administrators, as described in section 2.3. HUBzero infrastructure will be setup to automatically check for malware where appropriate by using:

  • Intrusion detection software
  • Anti-virus software (e.g., ClamAV)

2.1.1 Intrusion detection software

HUBzero shall rely on intrusion detection software selected and installed in the Sherlock environment.  In other environments, "Rootkit Hunter" will be deployed.  It (http://www.rootkit.nl/) aims to detect rootkits typically installed after a compromise. Scans shall be run at least weekly and whenever a compromise is suspected.

2.1.2 Anti-virus software

In the Sherlock environment, the anti-virus software is installed and managed by the Sherlock team as described in the Sherlock System Security Plan.  Any functionality described below that isn't covered by the Sherlock anti-virus solution, will be covered as described below.  In other environments:

a. Updates of anti-virus signatures

The anti-virus ClamAV signatures must be updated at least daily.  Normally this is done automatically by clamav-freshclam.

b. Downloadable resources

A weekly cron script must trigger a ClamAV scan of a hub's downloadable resources, and report any findings via email to system administrators.  System administrators must determine if the results are valid and remove infected files.

c. Incoming mail

Mail server software (e.g., exim, postfix) must be configured to scan incoming emails with an anti-virus such as ClamAV, and reject emails and attachments containing detected malware.

d. HTTP Uploads

The HUBzero science gateway web application must use the ClamAV daemon to automatically scan HTTP(S) uploads on the fly, and reject uploads containing detected malware.

e. Home directories of users

The home directories of users must be scanned monthly for malware with ClamAV.  It isn't practical to use a shorter scanning interval because on some hubs, scanning home directories takes more than a week.  Detected malware will either be deleted by a system administrator, or the user will be notified of the issue.  If by the next scan, the user hasn't taken action, a system administrator will delete the infected files.

 

2.2 What to do about malicious software

In the Sherlock HIPAA environment, malicious software will be handled by the Sherlock team as described in Sherlock policies.  Outside of it:

a. How to report malicious software

All events that may constitute IT Incidents should be reported to abuse@help.hubzero.org , and escalated to parent organizations as needed. More details on what constitutes an IT Incident and what to report are described in the HUBzero Incident Response Plan.

b. How to recover from malicious software

Once an infection has been determined to have occurred, the infected system should be taken offline (shutdown) as soon as possible. The ongoing risks to other infrastructure and users are a greater concern to HUBzero than the preservation of evidence achieved by examining the live system.

Malicious software can be extremely resistant to removal. Most often, wiping the hard drive, re-partitioning and complete OS installation from a trusted source is required, or is more effective than trying to fight the malware. The time necessary to decide whether this is required is often better spent in performing the procedure. However, HUBzero system administrators should attempt to determine the method by which the malicious software was installed. This is better done by looking at backups. Once a counter-measure has been determined, it should be applied to existing systems as well as to the rebuilt one as soon as possible.

2.3 Training

Developers are encouraged to attend security tracks at conferences, pursue independent reading and watch webcasts. In addition, the "UC Learning Center" offers a large number of security-related classes that all HUBzero staff should pursue.  A record of security training will be kept at https://help.hubzero.org/groups/policies/wiki/sec_training

The previously described practices and procedures will be taught to HUBzero system administrators. This will be done by assigned reading of this wiki and discussion.

3. Login Monitoring

Given that HUBzero has been designed as a 24/7 research environment; that accesses can presumably and justifiably occur at any time 24/7, and have been observed to occur at any time; that users include neophytes that often forget passwords and require many attempts for a valid login; that HUBzero workforce members have little knowledge of the habits of the clientele of a particular hub; login discrepancies are extremely difficult to identify and any such identification is error-prone. Therefore, HUBzero will make available to hub owners web login data and SSH login data on the systems belonging to that hub. Hub owners are responsible for monitoring logins to applications manipulating EPHI, and identifying discrepancies.

HUBzero’s contribution to login monitoring will be limited to providing automated protection against password guessing attacks.  This currently takes the form of temporary account lockout supplemented by the banning of IP addresses responsible for the lockout of several accounts.  Procedures to configure the lockout parameters and temporary bans will be documented.

4. Password Management

This is addressed by UCSD policy via the yearly "UC Cyber Security Awareness" training. Hubs deploying custom applications and Hub partners with other software are responsible for reminding users about password protection when accessing EPHI information.

title: Outgoing email via Amazon SES
content:
The Sherlock environment doesn't allow outgoing emails.  In order to send emails, we use Amazon SES.  For example, we need to notify users of ticket updates.  The confidentiality of tickets is preserved on HIPAA-covered hubs by not emailing the contents of the tickets, and only sending notices that there were updates to the ticket (this is a configuration item).   The connection to Amazon SES is done as follows:

1. Request Port 587 to be allowed through the Sherlock HTTP proxy to the Amazon SES SMTP server we are using "email-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com" .

2. Install the required SASL packages

3. Configure Postfix on the hub host to relay email to the AWS STMP server via port 587 with the appropriate AWS SES username and SASL password and the following options. 

SASL options:
smtp_sasl_auth_enable = yes
smtp_sasl_security_options = noanonymous
smtp_sasl_password_maps = hash:/etc/postfix/sasl_passwd
smtp_use_tls = yes
smtp_tls_security_level = encrypt
smtp_tls_note_starttls_offer = yes
smtp_tls_CAfile = /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt

title: Google Authentication
content:
"Sign in with Google" implemented by HUBzero uses OAuth 2.0 as follows:

  • The majority of the code uses the Google API Client library provided by Google (/libraries/google-api-php-client).  The google php client library follows the standard OAuth2 protocol.  
  • All of our customers should have separate client ids/secrets as the Google api console requires the redirect domain to match the application domain.  These (client ID and client secret) are stored as plugin param values (params are a JSON encoded string in the 'params' field of the #__extensions database table).
  • It doesn't use a refresh token. Refresh tokens apply primarily to longer lived access to the Google api.  Because we only make one call (to the authentication endpoint), which by definition includes explicate authentication from the user, the need for a refresh token is irrelevant.  The refresh token would come into play if, for example, people were able to do other google related api actions (like posting something to their google plus account) without explicitly authenticating for each action.
  • The access token is stored in the user's session data.

Source: Shawn Rice and Samuel Wilson in https://help.hubzero.org/support/ticket/8064

title: Shibboleth
content:
Shibboleth is deployed using packages from a Linux Operating System's repositories, for example the libapache2_mod_shib2 in Debian Linux.  This module handles the SAML-based communication between the hub and the single sign-on providers, and places any user attributes that were established across a login into the environment variables for the request. These variables consist of users' email addresses at the SSO institution, their names, and an eduPersonPrincipalName, which is basically a username on the providers domain. Of these, only the last is required but the others can be used as shortcuts to fill in registration fields on the hub.

(attributes exchanged: https://spaces.internet2.edu/display/InCFederation/Research+and+Scholarship+Attribute+Bundle)
(module documentation, the only configuration we use is to require a valid user for the /login/shibboleth url: https://wiki.shibboleth.net/confluence/display/SHIB2/NativeSPApacheConfig)

In addition to the Apache module, the package includes a daemon that is configured separately (/etc/shibboleth/shibboleth2.xml)

Our configuration of this part of the service is as-shipped, except that we configure the service to use InCommon's metadata to federate with SSO services in the research and scholarship category (and as a special case with NIH):

       <MetadataProvider type="XML" uri="https://wayf.incommonfederation.org/InCommon/InCommon-metadata.xml" backingFilePath="federation-metadata.xml" reloadInterval="7200">
           <MetadataFilter type="RequireValidUntil" maxValidityInterval="2419200"/>
           <MetadataFilter type="Signature" certificate="inc-md-cert.pem"/>
       </MetadataProvider>

This configuration is in accordance with the service agreement with InCommon.

Additionally we add routing through our content management system code for the redirect stage of user login:

           <SSO discoveryProtocol="SAMLDS" ECP="true" discoveryURL="https://nciphub.org/login?authenticator=shibboleth&wayf">
                  SAML2 SAML1
           </SSO>
           <SessionInitiator type="Chaining" Location="/login/shibboleth" isDefault="true" id="Login">
               <SessionInitiator type="SAML2" template="bindingTemplate.html"/>
               <SessionInitiator type="Shib1"/>
               <SessionInitiator type="SAMLDS" URL="https://nciphub.org/login?authenticator=shibboleth&wayf"/>
           </SessionInitiator>

What this does is to set up that URL on the hub as a service that answers the question "where do I redirect a user requesting to log in with this particular entity ID?" The Shibboleth software is capable of doing something like this without the intermediate step but we'd like to check in with the content management system's database to be sure that any given entity is enabled, a precaution that helps us avoid offering logins through institutions that will not supply the required EPPN attribute or that misbehave in any other way.

(documentation about this configuration file: https://wiki.shibboleth.net/confluence/display/SHIB2/NativeSPShibbolethXML)

Finally, there is public-facing configuration, which can find in its entirety by searching for nciphub in the InCommon metadata here: https://wayf.incommonfederation.org/InCommon/InCommon-metadata.xml

This is pretty standard, containing a note about our research & scholarship affiliation, which enables more providers to release attributes to us, the technical information needed by their software to interface with us (public key and endpoint URLs), some user-facing information like the site name, description, and support contacts, and the list of the attributes our service is interested in.

Source:  Description provided by Steven Snyder, author of the Shibboleth plugin, at https://help.hubzero.org/support/ticket/8065

title: External Information System Services
content:
- REQUIRED for FISMA COMPLIANCE, DO NOT MOVE OR DELETE -

This documents how HUBzero connects to external information system services, and implements parts of controls SA-5 and SA-9.  Sub-pages document a specific external service or connection mechanism to external services, e.g., Shibboleth, Google Auth, Amazon SES.

title: (SI) System and Information Integrity
content:
This is not a policy document. 

This document provides the implementation status for controls, in relation to responsibilities of HUBzero and the providers of the environments we are using (e.g., Sherlock).

For HIPAA-covered hubs, please refer to the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan as well.  The HUBzero controls below apply to all hubs unless contradicted by the Sherlock SSP or unapplicable or irrelevant due to the controls implemented in the Sherlock environment.

 

SI-1 System and Information Integrity Policy and Procedures

The HUBzero policy "164.312 c Integrity" mandates the implementation of control SI-1.  See the HUBzero Incident Response Plan under "3.2.3 Detective Measures": monitoring, anti-virus, scans, hashes

SI-2 Flaw Remediation

Control description:

The organization:
a. Identifies, reports, and corrects information system flaws;
b. Tests software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects before installation;
c. Installs security-relevant software and firmware updates promptly, in accordance with the note below, of the release of the updates; and
d. Incorporates flaw remediation into the organizational configuration management process.

Note: The timelines to remediate vulnerabilities is designated by the NIH Information Security Program. The following remediation timelines must be met, or the affected device may be removed from the network:
• Critical within 30 days;
• High within 60 days;
• Medium within 1 year; and
• Low within 1 year.

Implementation details

The HUBzero policy "164.312 c Integrity" mandates the implementation of control SI-2.  This is addressed in the Incident Response Plan, "3.3 Preventative Measures":Software Updates, as well as the policy on "Code Deployment" at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/code-deployment.  The procedure for web application vulnerability scanning is documented at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/procedures/technical/web-application-vulnerability-scanning along with the timelines required by this control.

Historical, for reference only: 

In the Purdue environment with Ogre configuration control, all patches are automatically applied the day of the release to non-production systems. Updates are checked daily, and the patches are applied next business day manually.

SI-3 Malicious Code Protection

Control description:

The organization:
a. Employs malicious code protection mechanisms at information system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code;
b. Updates malicious code protection mechanisms whenever new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures;
c. Configures malicious code protection mechanisms to:
1. Perform periodic scans of the information system at least monthly and real-time scans of files from external sources at endpoint and network entry/exit points as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed in accordance with organizational security policy; and
2. Executes one or more of the following in response to malicious code detection:
• Blocks malicious code
• Quarantines malicious code
• Sends an alert to the System Administrator; and
d. Addresses the receipt of false positives during malicious code detection and eradication and the resulting potential impact on the availability of the information system.

Note: Malicious code protection can include, for example, anti-virus agents and signature definitions, as well as reputation-based technologies.

Implementation details

The Sherlock environment is protected by a deployment of Sentinel One as described in the Sherlock System Security Plan (SSP).  In addition, the HUBzero science gateway web application uses ClamAV as described in policy "a 5 Security Awareness and Training", in section "2. Protection From Malicious Software".  The combination meets the requirements of this control.

SI-4 System and Information Integrity

Control description:

The organization:
a. Monitors the information system to detect:
1. Attacks and indicators of potential attacks in accordance with NIH and IC monitoring objectives as described AU-2 and AU-5(2) and
2. Unauthorized local, network, and remote connections (For Moderate and High systems: twice weekly);
b. Identifies unauthorized use of the information system through NIH and/or IC techniques and methods as described in AU-6 and AU-7(1);
c. Deploys monitoring devices: (i) strategically within the information system to collect organization-determined essential information; and (ii) at ad hoc locations within the system to track specific types of transactions of interest to the organization;
d. Protects information obtained from intrusion-monitoring tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion;
e. Heightens the level of information system monitoring activity whenever there is an indication of increased risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation based on law enforcement information, intelligence information, or other credible sources of information;
f. Obtains legal opinion with regard to information system monitoring activities in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, or regulations; and
g. Provides information system monitoring information to NIH Threat Mitigation and Incident Response (TMIR) and System Owners and IC ISSO, System Owners, and security personnel at either an as needed basis and/or, at a minimum, twice weekly for Moderate and High systems.

Implementation details

The HUBzero policy "164.312 c Integrity" mandates the implementation of control SI-4.

SI-5 Security Alerts and Advisories

Control description:

The organization:
a. Receives information system security alerts, advisories, and directives from the United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team (US-CERT) on an ongoing basis;
b. Generates internal security alerts, advisories, and directives as deemed necessary;
c. Disseminates security alerts, advisories, and directives to NIH CIO, CISO, TMIR and IC CIO, ISSO, System Owner, and security personnel; and
d. Implements security directives in accordance with established time frames or notifies the issuing organization of the degree of noncompliance.

Implementation details

The HUBzero policy "164.312 c Integrity" mandates the implementation of control SI-5.  See Incident Response Plan, "3.3 Preventative Measures": Advisories. 

SI-12 Information Handling and Retention

Control description:

The organization handles and retains information within the information system and information output from the system in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and operational requirements.

Implementation details

The HUBzero policy "164.312 c Integrity" mandates the implementation of control SI-12.

title: (SC) Systems and Communications Protection
content:
This is not a policy document. 

This document describes implementation details for controls, i.e., control requirements in comparison to implementation status in relation to responsibilities of HUBzero and the providers of the environments we are using (e.g., Sherlock).

SC-1 System and Communications Protection Policy and Procedures

Current Implementation Details:

This policy is documented in the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan.  HUBzero complies with this control with its Incident Response Plan,  Disaster Recovery Plan, and other systematically developed policies and procedures to cover HIPAA requirements. Communications protection is specifically covered under the HUBzero policy “164.312 Technical Safeguards, e Transmission Security” available at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/policies/mapping-to-national-standards-and-regulations/hipaa-view/164312-technical-safeguards/164312-e-transmission-security .

SC-5 Denial of Service Protection

Control Description:

The information system protects against or limits the effects of the following types of denial of service attacks:

  • Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) floods:
    • Smurf attack
    • Ping of death
    • Ping flood
  • Teardrop attack
  • Peer-to-peer attacks
  • Permanent DoS attack (i.e., phlashing)
  • Application level floods:
    • Internet Relay Chat (IRC) floods
    • Banana attack
    • Buffer overflow
  • Nuke
  • Distributed DoS attack
  • Reflected attack
  • Unintentional attack
  • DoS Level II

Note: NIH and the ICs refers to the NIST SP 800-61, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide and timely industry information on denial of service attacks to define additional and update existing security safeguards, as required.

Current Implementation Details:

The Sherlock SSP states that: "Customer compute systems are located on separate physical or logical systems from Sherlock management systems. VLAN and firewall segmentation shall be used to partition the network traffic and access of the different customer computing systems from Sherlock management systems. For Cloud systems virtualization will be performed using cloud virtualization tools (e.g., AWS Virtual Private Network (VPC))."  Preventative measures described in the HUBzero Incident Response Plan also harden the VMs received from Sherlock, setting the appropriate Linux kernel networking options, and implementing appropriate host firewall rules.

 

SC-13 Cryptographic Protection

The information system implements cryptographic mechanisms as defined in the HHS Standard for Encryption of Computing Devices and Information in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards.

Current Implementation Details:

The Sherlock SSP states that the "environment shall only use FIPS-validated cryptography products."  The HUBzero policy "164.312 e Transmission Security" implements best practices related to this control.

SC-15 Collaborative Computing Devices

The information system:
a. Prohibits remote activation of collaborative computing devices with no exceptions; and
b. Provides an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.

Current Implementation Details:

The Sherlock SSP states that "use of remote control software is prohibited within the Sherlock environment. Use of collaborative computing devices (network white boards, cameras, microphones, etc.) is also prohibited within the Sherlock network."  The HUBzero web application has no knowledge of or control over the client selected by users.

title: (SA) Systems and Services Acquisition
content:
(SA-1) System and Services Acquisition Policy and Procedures

Description in NCI template: "The organization:
a. Develops, documents, and disseminates to personnel/roles identified in Appendix A: Roles and Responsibilities the NIH Information Security (InfoSec)
Policy Handbook:
1. A system and services acquisition policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and
2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the system and services acquisition policy and associated system and services acquisition controls; and
b. Reviews and, if necessary, updates the current:
1. System and services acquisition policy at least every three (3) years; and
2. System and services acquisition procedures at least every three (3) years."

Implementation Description:  All required federal acquisition security language is reviewed by the respective issuing government agency ISSO both in initial solicitation and contract award stages for compliance with FISMA, Section 508, and privacy requirements. Internally, Sherlock and HUBzero rely on the SDSC (San Diego Supercomputing Center) acquisition and procurement policies and procedures, supplemented with the policies and procedures described in the following subsections and in the Sherlock System Security Plan.

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "All require (sic) federal acquisition security language is reviewed by the respective issuing government agency ISSO both in initial solicitation and contract award stages for compliance with FISMA, Section 508, and privacy requirements. Internally, HUBzero relies on Purdue acquisition and procurement policies and procedures and the Ariba purchasing system. A summary of these acquisition policies will be provided upon request."

(SA-2) Allocation of Resources

Description in NCI template: "The organization:

a. Determines information security requirements for the information system or information system service in mission/business process planning;

b. Determines, documents, and allocates the resources required to protect the information system or information system service as part of its capital planning and investment control process; and

c. Establishes a discrete line item for information security in organizational programming and budgeting documentation."

Implementation Description: (Partially in place) The decision to deploy hosted hubs in one of several available environments is based on security requirements.  Deploying HIPAA-covered hubs in the security-oriented Sherlock environment results in the proper resources being determined, documented and allocated for NCIhub.  HUBzero has a line item for the Sherlock environment.  However, HUBzero doesn't have a discrete line item covering information security in organizational programming and budgeting documentation, separate from the Sherlock environment. 

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "HUBzero must determine information security requirements for the information system with respect to mission/business process planning. Organizational programming and budgeting documentation must have a discrete line item for information security. Renewal documents for NCIPhub will contain a line item for charges in information security."

(SA-3) Life Cycle Support

Description in NCI template: "The organization:

a. Manages the information system using [Assignment: a formally defined and documented system development life cycle (SDLC) process] that incorporates information security considerations;

b. Defines and documents information security roles and responsibilities throughout the system development life cycle;

c. Identifies individuals having information security roles and responsibilities; and

d. Integrates the organizational information security risk management process into system development life cycle activities.

Note: The organization may formally define and document its own SDLC process; however, at a minimum, the process must conform to HHS Department-wide SDLC requirements (including the HHS Enterprise Performance Life Cycle (EPLC)). The organization may adopt the Department-wide SDLC or customize it to meet additional, organization-specific requirements."

Implementation Description:  HUBzero has a batch and revision process to push code to production.  The code deployment schedule is documented at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/code-deployment and the code deployment itself is automated with an Ansible playbook. Code repository policies are documented at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/coderepospolicies and define which code repositories are approved for use, and which are publicly accessible.

Individuals having information security roles and responsibilities are identified in the Incident Response Plan and the Emergency Contact Information document.  The integration of security risk management into the SDLC activities consist of:

  • All software is managed by a version control system.
  • The web application scanner "Detectify" (detectify.com) is employed monthly and before every major release.
  • Yearly Sherlock audits include a scan of the NCIhub science gateway.

Sherlock's management of the underlying infrasctructure and operating systems uses monthly package updates and reboots, staggered between non-production systems and production systems.

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "HUBzero has a batch and revision process to push to production. All software is managed by a version control system. IBM Appscan is employed before every major release. Yearly audits include a scan of the site."

(SA-4) Acquisition Process

Description in NCI template: "The organization includes the following requirements, descriptions, and criteria, explicitly or by reference, in the acquisition contract for the information system, system component, or information system service in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, guidelines, and organizational mission/business needs:

a. Security functional requirements;

b. Security strength requirements;

c. Security assurance requirements;

d. Security-related documentation requirements;

e. Requirements for protecting security-related documentation;

f. Description of the information system development environment and environment in which the system is intended to operate; and

g. Acceptance criteria.

Note: Required security configurations and settings should also be included (see SA-4 c.e.5).
"

Explanation: This is about providing to the hub owner documentation describing the properties of the security controls to be employed within the hub, in sufficient detail to permit analysis and testing of the controls.

Implementation Description: SDSC HUBzero will provide to the hub owner the hub's system security plan, configuration management plan, system diagram, data flow diagram, and contingency plan, which will cover the above

SA-4 (10) Control Enhancement: Use of Approved PIV Products

Description in NCI template: "The organization employs only information technology products on the FIPS 201-approved products list for Personal Identity Verification (PIV) capability implemented within organizational information systems."

Implementation Description: SDSC HUBzero does not have a PIV capability. However, the NIH login web site will be used via SAML, therefore conforming to NIH security requirements. This will be implemented via the Shibboleth software. Internally, SDSC HUBzero uses Multi-Factor Authentication.

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "HUBzero software supports several authentication mechanisms, including the use of Shibboleth identity federation. Upon NCIP's request, password-based authentication can be disabled and Shibboleth configured to use approved authentication providers."

(SA-5) Information System Documentation

Description in NCI template: "The organization:
a. Obtains administrator documentation for the information system, system component, or information system service that describes:
1. Secure configuration, installation, and operation of the system, component, or service;
2. Effective use and maintenance of security functions/mechanisms; and
3. Known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative (i.e., privileged) functions;
b. Obtains user documentation for the information system, system component, or information system service that describes:
1. User-accessible security functions/mechanisms and how to effectively use those security functions/mechanisms;
2. Methods for user interaction, which enables individuals to use the system, component, or service in a more secure manner; and
3. User responsibilities in maintaining the security of the system, component, or service;
c. Documents attempts to obtain information system, system component, or information system service documentation when such documentation is either unavailable or nonexistent and recreates selected information system documentation if such documentation is essential to the effective implementation and/or operation of security controls;
d. Protects documentation as required, in accordance with the risk management strategy; and
e. Distributes documentation to NIH and/or IC System Owners, System Administrators, Network Administrators, Data Owners, Business Owners, Project Managers, Service Area Managers, and other personnel as appropriate."

Implementation Description: This is addressed by the HUBzero documentation maintained at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation and the Web server security model  for the filesystem.  In addition, HUBzero uses Ansible playbooks and roles with configuration tasks and configuration file templates which are easily understandable and stored in git revision control.

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "Addressed by HUBzero documentation (hubzero.org), Web server security model (HUBzero Web Server Filesystem Security Policy) at https://hubzero.org/groups/policies/resources"

(SA-9) External Information System Services

Description in NCI template: "The organization:
a. Requires that providers of external information system services comply with organizational information security requirements and employ HHS, NIH, and IC security controls and comply with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance;
b. Formally defines and documents government oversight and user roles and responsibilities with regard to external information system services in a service level agreement (SLA) or similar agreement; and
c. Employs processes, methods, and techniques as documented in contracts, service level agreements, and other agreements to monitor security control compliance by external service providers on an ongoing basis."

Implementation Description: HUBzero and Sherlock will follow the NCI SSP template's policy text with regards to external information system services.  The SSP template text has assignments made by NCI to the SP 800-53 controls, to make sure we use the appropriate HHS, NIH, and IC security controls.  Examples of external information services are the use of Amazon SES for outgoing email, the use of Shibboleth to connect to various identity service providers approved by NCI, or the use of Google Auth for authentication.  Our use of external information system services is documented in HUBzero documentation at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/external-information-system-services . 

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "Shibboleth software (https://shibboleth.net/) will be deployed to integrate authentication. A policy will be written for NCIPHub. Currently shared Google OAuth authentication is in production. Documentation will be provided as per tickets 8063 and 8064."

Note about the historical text:  these were actually

  • https://help.hubzero.org/support/ticket/8064 Google auth
  • https://help.hubzero.org/support/ticket/8065  Shibboleth

(SA-15) Development Process, Standards, and Tools (not FISMA Low)

HUBzero has a contribution guide and a style guide, covering topics such as PHP coding style, naming conventions, CSS coding style, database schema conventions and commit messages.  The use of the tool "PHP CodeSniffer" is recommended.

  • style guide: https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/22/webdevs/conventions
  • contribution guide: https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/current/webdevs/index/contributions

title: (PS) Personnel Security
content:
PS-1 Personnel Security Policy and Procedures

SDSC HUBzero relies on SDSC Human Resources for personnel security, supplemented with additional procedures and policies as described below.  The Sherlock policy is documented in the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan. SDSC complies with all UC San Diego and UC personnel controls and applicable federal and state laws and regulations.

PS-2 Position Risk Designation

All SDSC staff with access to the Sherlock environment are able to access the sensitive data hosted within the Sherlock environment, are therefore assigned the same risk designation, and are subject to background checks prior to system access. Per both Amazon and Microsoft, they conduct criminal background checks, as permitted by law, as part of pre-employment screening practices for employees and commensurate with the employee’s position and level of access.

PS-3 Personnel Screening

All SDSC staff with access to the Sherlock environment must first successfully pass an identity and criminal check prior to access approval. Per both Amazon and Microsoft, they conduct criminal background checks, as permitted by law, as part of pre-employment screening practices for employees and commensurate with the employee’s position and level of access.

HUBzero relies on SDSC's Human Resources policies and procedures.

PS-4 Personnel Termination

1. HUBzero Employees: Access privileges to the science gateway web application will be removed or disabled as soon as possible upon notification from an employee’s supervisor that the access is no longer needed.
2. Hub users with elevated privileges: Access credentials in the science gateway web application will be removed or disabled as soon as possible upon notification from a credible and authoritative source (e.g., the owner of a hub) that the access is no longer needed or that it should be withdrawn.  If applicable, HUBzero staff will notify Sherlock staff, via email, of any users who are terminated or transferred. Sherlock staff disable accounts within one business day of notification.
3. SDSC Employees: SDSC terminates information system access; conducts exit interviews; retrieves all security-related organizational information and system-related property; and retains access to organizational information and information systems formerly controlled by the terminated individual.

Detailed HUBzero termination procedures are documented at https://help.hubzero.org/groups/production/wiki/TerminationProcs

PS-5 Personnel Transfer

SDSC reviews logical and physical access authorizations to information systems/facilities when personnel are reassigned or transferred to other positions within the organization and ensures accurate assignment of privileges.  Additionally, this is addressed by HUBzero under the policy to grant and review access to systems. Personnel roles are defined in the webserver security model. Full details can be found at:

https://help.hubzero.org/groups/hubzero_hipaa/wiki/164308a3WorkforceSecurity

PS-6 Access Agreements

Sherlock policies are defined in the Sherlock SSP.  Hub users must agree to an initial terms of use, e.g., https://ncihub.org/aboutus/terms, which includes an Abuse Policy (see https://ncihub.org/legal/abuse).  Hubs have functionality to force users to agree again to the terms of use;  hub administrators can trigger this whenever the terms of use change, or every year.

PS-7 Third-Party Personnel Security

Any subcontractor with unsupervised access to the Sherlock environment is subject to the same background check requirements as SDSC staff.  HUBzero, as part of SDSC, utilizes the same HR procedures.

PS-8 Personnel Sanctions

SDSC staff are subject to sanctions, as defined in UC policy, if it is determined that they are non-compliant with Sherlock or HUBzero policies.

title: (PL) Planning
content:
PL-1 Security Planning Policy and Procedures

Security planning policies and procedures are defined as found on hubzero.org documentation under "Information Technology Policies, Procedures and Resources".

PL-2 System Security Plan

System security plans (SSPs) appropriate to support FISMA certification of specific hubs will be developed from the NCI templates provided at https://wiki.nci.nih.gov/display/NSCI/FISMA+Security+Templates+and+Forms, and will be stored on hubzero.org and on the hub in question.  There can likely be variations between the plans of different hubs, due to different security requirements, FISMA certification levels, and assignments made to controls by the certifying federal organization, so multiple SSPs are to be expected, with a common core provided in this documentation.


The SSPs developed by HUBzero will build on the Sherlock SSP and will:

1. Be consistent with the organizations enterprise architecture;

2. Explicitly define the authorization boundary for the system;

3. Describe the operational context of the information system in terms of missions and business processes;

4. Provide the security categorization of the information system including supporting rationale;

5. Describe the operational environment for the information system and relationships with or connections to other information systems;

6. Provide an overview of the security requirements for the system;

7. Identify any relevant overlays, if applicable;

8. Describe the security controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements including a rationale for the tailoring decisions; and

9. Be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to plan implementation;

b. Be distributed, as well as subsequent changes, to the NIH CIO, CISO, System Owners, and NIH ISAO at the enterprise level and IC CIO, ISSO; System Owner, and IC InfoSec Program at the IC level;

c. Be reviewed every 365 days or when significant changes occur;

d. Be updated to address changes to the information system/environment of operation or problems identified during plan implementation or security control assessments; and

e. Be protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

PL-4 Rules of Behavior

"Control: The organization:
a.  Establishes and makes readily available to individuals requiring access to the information system, the rules that describe their responsibilities and expected behavior with regard to information and information system usage;
b.  Receives a signed acknowledgment from such individuals, indicating that they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules of behavior, before authorizing access to information and the information system;
c.  Reviews and updates the rules of behavior [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; and
d.  Requires individuals who have signed a previous version of the rules of behavior to read and re-sign when the rules of behavior are revised/updated."

When users sign up for an account, they must agree to terms of use before they are granted an account. The implementation of signed acknowledgments is not feasible for non-organizational users. Instead, and in accordance with NIST 800-53, this control can be satisfied for non-organizational users through System Use Notification (AC-8) as well as through required security awareness training if such training includes rules of behavior.

title: (MP) Media Protection
content:
This policy is documented in the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan.  For HIPAA-covered hubs, HUBzero has no additional policies or procedures for these controls.

 

As HUBzero doesn't handle physical servers directly anymore, responsibility for this family of controls is delegated.  See also "164.310 Physical Safeguards, d Device and Media Controls"

For historical purposes, HUBzero also had this policy when handling physical servers:

(Historical) MP-6 MEDIA SANITIZATION

Control: The organization:
     a.  Sanitizes [Assignment: organization-defined information system media] prior to disposal, release out of organizational control, or release for reuse using [Assignment: organization-defined sanitization techniques and procedures] in accordance with applicable federal and organizational standards and policies; and
     b.  Employs sanitization mechanisms with the strength and integrity commensurate with the security category or classification of the information.

HUBzero’s media sanitization procedures are described in "Disposal for Electronic-Based Media" at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/infosec/procedures/technical/disposal-for-electronic-based-media . These procedures satisfy the Purdue’s “Media Disposal Guidelines“ documented at https://www.purdue.edu/securepurdue/bestPractices/mediaDisposalGuidelines.html by using the “enhanced secure erase” or, if not available, “secure erase” hard drive functionality, or 3-pass DoD erasure, physically destructing storage devices or reusing media (after wiping) only within HUBzero. Hard drives replaced under warranty for servers with FISMA or HIPAA requirements are also subjected to the “enhanced secure erase” or “secure erase” operation, whenever possible, before shipping to Dell by courrier. However, these operations are not guaranteed to succeed on faulty drives. To maximize the likelihood of "secure erase"-type operations succeeding, whenever possible HUBzero replaces drives as soon as predictive failures are detected, before the device fails completely.

title: (PE) Physical and Environmental Protection
content: Controls PE-1 to PE-18 are addressed in the Sherlock environment as described in the Sherlock System Security Plan.  Please refer to it, as HUBzero uses these facilities unmodified.

title: (IR) Incident Response
content:
Most of the controls are addressed in the incident response plan.  Below are supplemental details.

IR-2 Incident Response Training

Control: The organization provides incident response training to information system users
consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities:
a.  Within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of assuming an incident response role
    or responsibility;
b.  When required by information system changes; and
c.  [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] thereafter.

Training is provided within one month of assuming an incident response role or responsibility, when required, and as needed thereafter.

IR-5 Incident Monitoring

Control: "The organization tracks and documents information system security incidents."


Information system security incidents are tracked and documented in the ticketing system.  The ticketing system has features that support this, such as private comments visible only to the hub administrators, and the capability to only send notifications that a ticket was changed without emailing sensitive details or the comments themselves.  In addition, the ticketing system provides statistics at the "/support/stats" URL.

IR-8  Incident Response Plan

For HIPAA-covered hubs, the Sherlock Program maintains an Incident Response Plan that is distributed & updated yearly (if needed).  HUBzero also has and maintains an IRP for HUBzero science gateways, which will engage the Sherlock IRP whenever an incident exceeds the scope of the HUBzero software or whenever HUBzero staff have difficulty responding or require support from the Sherlock team.

Incident response for other hubs is also described in the HUBzero team's IRP.

content:

  • Account Management Policies at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/policies/account-management

IA-8 Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users)

People can abuse a hub to by creating "spam" accounts, i.e., accounts abused to create blogs, profiles, projects or other content that promote some unrelated financial or illegal scheme, most often fraudulent.  One way to combat this is to limit the scope of account registration approval.  This can be phrased as "Email domains need to be screened during the account creation process."  One way to do that is, instead of auto-approving all accounts, accounts can be set to require manual approval, except accounts from some domains like .edu and .gov.  The plugin "User - Auto-Approve" ("autoapprove") can approve users with email addresses matching configurable domains:

 

Historical, for reference only: While at Purdue, HUBzero used Purdue's identification and authentication policy documented in the archived Authentication and Authorization (VII.B.1) which was superseded on July 15, 2019 by the standard on Authentication, Authorization and Access Controls (S-13).
